name: Org Strategy Decision Framework
description: Comprehensive framework for evaluating single-org vs. multi-org Salesforce architecture for pharma/life sciences enterprises. Based on four decision dimensions, an operating model quadrant, and a scenario matrix.
source: Org Strategy And Design — Salesforce Life Sciences

four_dimensions.description: Four dimensions for making org strategy decisions. Evaluate customers against all four before recommending single or multi-org.

sub_factors.description: Prioritize speed of innovation vs. managing common business processes in a common org.
Decide whether to handle complexity within an expanding single org or multiple new orgs.
Determine if standard business processes and data consistency are better achieved with single or multiple orgs.
Assess cost-effectiveness of implementing standards in single vs. multiple-org environments.
Consider complexity of managing standard requirements within a single org vs. multiple orgs.
Governance framework to ensure a common data model across business units.
Whether higher data volumes risk impacting performance in a single-org environment.
Ensure organizational buy-in to single-org strategy before implementing. Ensure enterprise architecture oversight exists.
Balance strong controls over multiple project teams in single org vs. individual controls per org.
Assess company maturity and readiness in handling change management for the chosen approach.
Fast deployment of shared functionality in single org vs. reuse of functionality across multiple orgs. Profile cost in single vs. multi-org.
Multi-level support in single org via integrated service desk vs. dedicated support teams per org.
Dedicated release management per org vs. centralized process across multiple orgs.

operating_model_quadrant.description: 2x2 matrix adapted from MIT CISR framework. X-axis: Business Process Standardization (Low→High). Y-axis: Business Process Integration (Low→High).

quadrants.name: Diversification
quadrants.definition: Independent business units with different customers and expertise.
quadrants.it_capability: Provide economies of scale without limiting independence.
quadrants.org_recommendation: Most likely always multiple orgs. Consolidating different business processes and data models into one org is usually very complicated.
quadrants.pharma_example: Separate pharma and consumer health divisions with no shared customers or processes.

quadrants.name: Coordination
quadrants.definition: Unique business units with a need to know each other's transactions.
quadrants.it_capability: Access to shared data through standard technology interfaces.
quadrants.org_recommendation: As few orgs as technically possible. High process integration requirements can be met with integration middleware. Single org value is much higher. Use multiple profiles in fewer orgs to keep LOBs orchestrated.
quadrants.pharma_example: Commercial and Medical Affairs sharing HCP accounts but running different engagement processes.

quadrants.name: Replication
quadrants.it_capability: Provide standard infrastructure and application components for global efficiencies.
quadrants.org_recommendation: Multiple orgs, but deploy unlocked packages from a central org into all replicated BUs. Maintain standard processes with local control/administration.
quadrants.pharma_example: Country affiliates running identical commercial processes independently — same workflows, no cross-country data needs.

quadrants.name: Unification
quadrants.definition: Single business with global process standards and global data access.
quadrants.it_capability: Enterprise systems reinforcing standard processes and providing global data access.
quadrants.org_recommendation: As few orgs as possible. Use multiple profiles within the same org rather than one profile per org.
quadrants.pharma_example: Global commercial operations with shared KOL lists, global sample tracking, and unified reporting across all affiliates.

scenario_matrix.description: Implementation scenario matrix. Cross-reference Data Sharing requirements against Governance model to determine the starting recommendation.

axes.rows: Data Sharing: Required | Not Required | Not Allowed
